s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic papular eruption of the extremities with a chronic time course
salient_findings: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on the extremities
Erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
3-month history of symptoms
No remarkable medical or family history
No concurrent medications
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa not involved
Normal laboratory tests, including blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor
Skin biopsy showed mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

raw.syndrome_frame: Pruritic papular eruption of the extremities with a chronic time course
salient_findings: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on the extremities
Erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
3-month history of symptoms
No remarkable medical or family history
No concurrent medications
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa not involved
Normal laboratory tests, including blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor
Skin biopsy showed mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of intensively pruritic papules, skin biopsy showing mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis, along with the presence of well-developed cornoid lamellae and individual cell dyskeratosis, are characteristic features of lichen planus.

rejected.label: Guttate psoriasis
rejected.why: The absence of typical psoriatic scale and the presence of individual cell dyskeratosis and vacuolar degeneration of the basal cell layer are not typical for guttate psoriasis

rejected.label: Phytophotodermatitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of exposure to plants or sunlight that would suggest phytophotodermatitis

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic orange-red hue and palmoplantar keratoderma of pityriasis rubra pilaris

rejected.label: Atopic dermatitis
rejected.why: The patient's age of onset and lack of personal or family history of atopy make atopic dermatitis less likely
